working_memory.text: Marisa Venn, the last working bookbinder in the county, has taken on an apprentice for the first time in her thirty-year career. The apprentice will spend two years learning to sew text blocks, pare leather and tool lettering by hand before being allowed to take customer work. Venn's shop repairs family bibles and rebinds worn library books, and she says demand has risen as people bring in books that cannot be replaced. The apprenticeship is funded partly by a heritage crafts grant.
